title: Combine named predicates to find eligible users

blocks.text: Predicates made from method references combine: `p.and(q)`, `p.or(q)`, `Predicate.not(p)`. The page builds its eligibility rule from two static helpers (`Eligibility::isAdult`, `Eligibility::hasEmail`) and a record accessor used as an unbound reference (`User::verified`), and collects to a typed array with `toArray(String[]::new)`.
`User` is a record `(String username, String email, boolean verified, int age)`. Complete `Eligibility`:

items: `static boolean isAdult(User u)`: the user is 18 or older.
`static boolean hasEmail(User u)`: the email is present and not blank.
`List<String> eligible(List<User> users)`: usernames of users who are adult **and** verified **and** have an email, in order.
`String[] unverified(List<User> users)`: usernames of the users who are not verified, in order.

blocks.text: Mind the boundary age, and the ways an email can be missing.

cases.says: It names the eligible users, and the unverified ones as a String array.
A user of exactly 18 is an adult.
An email of spaces only does not count as having an email.
A null email does not count as having one, and is checked without a NullPointerException.
Eligibility needs adult and verified and an email all at once; a verified minor with an email is not eligible.

concepts: Predicates built from static and unbound references combine with and, or and Predicate.not.
toArray(String[]::new) collects a stream into a String[] rather than an Object[].
